transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Today I'd like to give you a short history of cinema, from the first moving pictures to the arrival of colour and sound.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: The story begins in the 1890s. In 1895, the Lumière brothers in Paris showed the first public film screening to a paying audience. The films were very short, around fifty seconds, and they showed everyday scenes, such as workers leaving a factory. Audiences were amazed. People say that when a train arrived on the screen, some viewers ran from the room, although historians now doubt this story.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: In the early years, cinema was silent. A pianist or small orchestra played music in the theatre, and text cards told the audience what the characters said. Despite the lack of sound, silent films were very popular, and stars like Charlie Chaplin became famous around the world. By the 1920s, there were more than twenty thousand cinemas in the United States alone.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: The big change came in 1927 with The Jazz Singer, the first successful film with spoken dialogue. Within three years, most studios had stopped making silent films. Some actors lost their careers because their voices did not suit the new technology.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Colour arrived more slowly. Early colour processes were expensive and the results were often unnatural. It was not until the 1950s, when television became a threat, that studios used colour regularly to attract people back to the cinema.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Finally, let's look at how cinema changed in the digital age. Since about the year 2000, most films have been recorded and shown digitally, which is cheaper and allows special effects that were impossible before. On the other hand, some directors still prefer traditional film, because they believe it has a warmer look.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: For next week's seminar, please watch one silent film of your choice and note down three differences between it and a modern film.
